frameworksData.heading: The frameworks and models behind Edstellar's employee engagement consulting.
frameworksData.description: The employee engagement field is built on a body of established models. Edstellar's 5A method puts the most widely recognized ones to work.

items.name: Job Demands-Resources Model
items.author: Bakker & Demerouti
items.description: Engagement rises when job resources outweigh job demands.

phases.title: Balancing demands
phases.subtitle: Ease the load that drains people

phases.title: Burnout prevention
phases.subtitle: Spot and close the risk early

items.name: Self-Determination Theory
items.author: Deci & Ryan
items.description: People are motivated by autonomy, mastery and connection, not just rewards.

phases.title: Autonomy design
phases.subtitle: Give people real choice in how they work

items.name: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory
items.author: Frederick Herzberg
items.description: Hygiene factors stop dissatisfaction; motivators are what actually drive engagement.

items.name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
items.author: Abraham Maslow
items.description: People are engaged when lower needs are met and higher ones can be pursued.

items.name: Kahn's Model of Engagement
items.author: William Kahn
items.description: People engage when work feels meaningful, safe and they have the resources to give.

phases.title: Meaningfulness
phases.subtitle: Make the work feel worth it

phases.title: Psychological safety
phases.subtitle: Make it safe to bring themselves

phases.title: Availability
phases.subtitle: Free up the energy to engage

items.name: Job Characteristics Model
items.author: Hackman & Oldham
items.description: Five job traits create the meaning, responsibility and feedback that drive motivation.

phases.title: Job design

whyCtaData.heading: Ready for employee engagement that turns feeling into commitment?

items.question: What does employee engagement consulting include?
items.answer: It covers your engagement strategy and drivers, employee engagement surveys and pulse surveys, eNPS measurement, employee experience design, manager enablement, recognition and wellbeing, and the action planning and metrics that make engagement stick, all aligned to the business goals.

items.question: Is employee engagement the same as employee satisfaction?
items.answer: No. Satisfaction is how content people are; engagement is how committed and motivated they are to give their best. We build the drivers of engagement, purpose, managers, growth and voice, that move performance and retention, not just how people rate the perks.

items.question: How long does an employee engagement program take?
items.answer: Typically a baseline in four to six weeks, then an ongoing rhythm, because engagement is built and sustained over time, not fixed in a single project.

items.question: Do you help act on the results, not just run the survey?
items.answer: Yes. Manager enablement, recognition, listening and the action planning that turns feedback into change are the core of the engagement, so results lead to visible action.

items.question: What do we get at the end?
items.answer: An engagement strategy and driver map, a listening and eNPS baseline, an experience and manager plan, and the engagement metrics you own and run.
